messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [INCIDENT] Severity=high — serving-runtime in us-west-2 reporting gradual memory growth for ~6h. Multiple containers show CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY then crashloop. Affected pool: dedicated-gpu-pool-5. Start time ~2026-03-15T02:45Z. Incident ID INC-2045012345.

alice: ack — I'm on call. assigning eng-sre + eng-runtime. initial triage: symptoms point to paged-attention allocator fragmentation and slow KV cache growth. Collecting logs + metrics now.

brian: current counts: 47 OOMs in last 30m across nodes node-23,node-24,node-27. Error spike started ~02:40Z. grafana: http://grafana/redwood/d/abcd (embedding/generate error-rate panel)

sana: stack fragments from multiple containers look consistent: allocator failing to find contiguous slots then kvcache pins piling up. Example from node-24: 

```
[runtime] 02:41:12.345 ERROR paged_alloc_map.cpp:213 slot_alloc failed: required=8 pages, free_chunks=[1,2,1,3]
[kvcache] 02:41:12.347 WARN kv_cache_pin.cpp:78 leak suspected: pinned_pages=124, last_eviction=72m
[gpu] 02:41:12.350 ERROR cuda: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: tried alloc 512MB
```

sana: TL;DR: fragmentation + slow creeping ``kv_cache`` accumulation -> allocator can't fulfill larger contiguous allocations and we hit GPU OOM during attention paging.

kevin: immediate mitigations to reduce customer impact:
1) divert traffic from dedicated-gpu-pool-5 to hosted-fallback pool (smaller models / quantized variants)
2) temporarily disable continuous batching on the pool (reduces per-request allocation size)
3) force aggressive kvcache eviction threshold for the pool
4) schedule rolling restarts of the worst nodes to reclaim fragmented resources

alice: executing traffic shift now: `rdwctl route set --from dedicated-gpu-pool-5 --to hosted-fallback --percentage 100 --dry-run=false` — applying. Expect latency change ~+30-60ms.

incident-bot: Action logged: routing change applied by alice. Severity annotation updated.

sana: initiating kvcache eviction dry-run: `rdwctl kvcache evict --pool dedicated-gpu-pool-5 --threshold 30% --preview` — preview looks safe. Will apply eviction in 2 minutes.

brian: planning restarts: will do sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime on node-23 then wait 45s, node-24 then wait 45s, node-27. Rolling restart schedule posted to ops-runbook.

cs-bot: Customer impact: 12 customers in us-west-2 have reported timeouts for embeddings/generate endpoints in the last hour. Posting interim notification to affected customers. CS doc: https://redwood/cs/incidents/INC-2045012345

alice: running restarts now. monitoring error rate and latency.

[~10m later]

sana: after kvcache eviction + rolling restarts we observe OOMs fell from 47 -> 3 in 30m and crashloop backoffs stopped for node-23/node-24. Latency back toward baseline on routed traffic. Fragmentation metric still drifting (free contiguous pages ~3.2%).

kevin: good short-term. we need a longer-term fix: propose allocator coalescing pass + proactive defragmentation during idle windows and stricter per-request KV limits. I'll open a patch branch.

brian: archived mini heap-dumps and logs to S3 for postmortem: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2045012345/ (heap-dump-node-24.tar.gz, runtime-logs-node-23-24-27.tar.gz).

kevin: creating incident ticket INC-2045012345 in Jira and linking PR r/inference/runtime: `kv-defrag-hotfix`. Plan: canary to 10% traffic after tests, monitor for 2 hours, then roll.

sana: notes for postmortem: root cause hypothesis = paged allocator free-list fragmentation + many small KV pins preventing coalescing; allocator couldn't satisfy larger contiguous allocations used by paged attention, leading to GPU OOM. Action items:
- add coalescing pass on free list
- implement kvcache aggressive eviction when fragmentation metric > X%
- telemetry: per-model allocation size histogram to validate smaller models causing fragmentation pattern
- add metric alert for free-contiguous-pages < 5%

alice: handing off to daytime oncall @sana for monitoring and followups. Handoff at 09:00 PST tomorrow. Creating postmortem stub and assigning owners.

cs-bot: Customer update sent: "We observed elevated memory errors impacting some inference workloads in us-west-2. We diverted traffic and applied mitigations; a permanent fix is being developed. Next update in 2 hours or when we confirm hotfix canary."

sana: tentative ETA: hotfix canary in ~4hrs, full rollout after verification ~12hrs. Will update timeline in Jira.

alice: closing incident thread here; summary: short-term mitigations (traffic shift, kvcache eviction, rolling restarts) reduced OOMs and customer impact. Root cause likely allocator fragmentation + KV leak pattern. Owners and followups tracked in INC-2045012345. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2045012345 marked RESOLVED by alice (oncall). Postmortem pending.
